manifest.description: Measures a GitHub or GitLab repository before it changes it. Designs a calibrated performance metric (the ruler), proves the metric is trustworthy against a known win, then runs keep-or-revert improvement cycles: every candidate fix is written in an isolated worktree, gated against an edit allowlist and the repo's own tests, and kept only when the measured win clears the noise band. By default, survivors are drafted as GitHub pull requests or GitLab merge requests you review and publish yourself.
manifest.highlight_1: Proves its own metric first — a run refuses to start on an untrustworthy ruler
manifest.highlight_2: Every candidate is measured A/B, or RED/GREEN for bug fixes, never just 'looks right'
manifest.highlight_3: Keeps a change only when the win clears the measured noise band
manifest.highlight_4: Drafts GitHub pull requests or GitLab merge requests — draft-only, never published or merged for you
manifest.highlight_5: Works on a push-disabled clone, so nothing escapes the sandbox unreviewed
manifest.highlight_6: One resumable chat session per pull or merge request, finding, and run
manifest.use_case_1: Prove measurable performance gains or reproducible bug fixes before turning survivors into reviewable GitHub or GitLab changes.
manifest.configuration_1: The gateway host needs git and an authenticated GitHub CLI (gh) or GitLab CLI (glab); connect a repository, choose its base branch, and calibrate a ruler before performance runs.
